The worst network of veterinary clinics I've ever known. Dr. Ibanez is all about status.
My dog's story began in April 2024, when he started limping on his hind legs. At the time, he wasn't even a year old yet. While researching, I found excellent references about Dr. Fernando Ibanez and, luckily, he worked at WeVets, a network affiliated with my dog's health insurance plan.
From the first consultation, something caught my attention: Dr. Ibanez never sees patients alone, always accompanied by at least three students, and dedicates little or no direct attention to the animal. Consultations last an average of 20 minutes. He doesn't allow time for questions. Even with my dog ​​limping, he stated that, from an orthopedic point of view, there was no problem. He didn't request an MRI and stated that the x-ray was sufficient, claiming that, as a veterinarian, he knew there was no need for more in-depth examinations.

Without a precise diagnosis, he advised me to seek out a cardiologist, a hematologist, and a nephrologist. I followed all the instructions exactly. Several tests were performed over the course of months, and absolutely nothing was found.
During this period, we started a pain treatment with cannabis oil, widely supported by studies in modern medicine, but completely ignored by Dr. Ibanez. After starting the treatment, my dog ​​stopped limping and showing pain. Even so, he used extremely strong medications for pain control for months.
After seeing all the specialists indicated, as instructed by Dr. Ibanez himself, we returned for a consultation. My dog ​​continued to limp on his hind leg. Upon presenting the entire history and tests performed over almost 12 months, Dr. Ibanez suggested, for the first time, a possible disease… in the elbow of the front legs. Yes, front legs. He even suggested surgery on the front elbow, making it clear that the decision would be "entirely ours, at our own risk."
The question remains: why did he never take responsibility for a diagnosis? It became clear that he had no idea what was happening to our dog. We obviously opted not to perform any surgery.
At the end of 2025, my dog ​​began to have sporadic seizures. We sought out a neurologist, who was categorical: an MRI should have been done since 2024. According to him, this failure was serious, even more so considering that Dr. Ibanez had claimed that general anesthesia would be dangerous for my dog.
We had the MRI done in December 2025, and the result was devastating: several herniated discs. According to our current veterinarian, these hernias arose as a consequence of postural adaptation to the pain of a primary hernia, precisely the one that was never diagnosed by Dr. Ibanez. Today, my dog ​​has spinal deviation due to the number of hernias. According to the veterinarian, it is practically a miracle that he is still walking and "healthy."
Therefore, I leave here a sincere warning: if you love your dog, stay away from Dr. Fernando Ibanez and WeVets.
As if that weren't enough, WeVets also mutilated my father-in-law's newborn puppy due to misconduct by another veterinarian in the network. WeVets operates as a business, not as a provider of care. On several occasions, they insisted that my dog ​​be hospitalized, even though he was only limping.
In our case, we trusted Dr. Ibanez's status and reputation, and this cost our dog dearly in terms of health. What still comforts me is knowing that if he had identified the hernia in the past, he could have operated without proper criteria and possibly killed my dog.
Today, I will do absolutely everything in my power for his health. And I will definitely stay far away from WeVets, Aclivepa, Acco Veterinária, and anywhere else that has any connection with Dr. Fernando Ibanez.

I've been going there since 2021. It was great, it was humane. After the change to Wevets, everything changed. A procedure done in 2023 that cost me R$300.00 privately, because Petlove didn't cover it, is now being charged R$2800.00 privately. I understand that 3 years have passed, things get more expensive, the case isn't exactly the same, but from R$300.00 to R$2800.00?
And what's worse is not being able to resolve anything at the clinic anymore, having to depend on Wevets' concierge who only responds when they want to.

I also commend the cleanliness of the place; but on the day of the surgery, after the procedure was done, while I was already leaving with my pet, still weak from the anesthesia, they called me to the reception, and the receptionist, without any care, charged me in front of other people, even though I had already paid upon arrival.

Report for Complaint of Veterinary Negligence
On April 24, 2025, around 4 PM, I took my cat for emergency care at the Santana Veterinary Hospital, Wevets network.
After about two hours of waiting, I was seen by veterinarian Elen Beatriz Mesquita de Assis.
During the consultation, the professional limited herself to only visually observing the animal and placing it on the floor to analyze its locomotion, without performing basic clinical procedures such as listening to the heartbeat, checking body temperature, assessing hydration, or performing any detailed physical examination.
Even after I clearly reported symptoms such as lack of appetite, weakness, and abnormal behavior, such as outbursts of cries of pain, the animal was discharged without any complementary examination or prescribed medication, as she claimed it was normal.

Unfortunately, the following day (April 25, 2025), my cat had a seizure and died on the way to the hospital, showing that there was a serious condition that was not diagnosed or even investigated by the professional.

Therefore, I am filing a complaint for negligence and requesting that the responsibilities for the failure in care be investigated, which, by all indications, directly contributed to the fatal outcome.
I received excellent service.

It's difficult to find good veterinarians these days. I only went to get my cat vaccinated, but the establishment has zero safety precautions for cats; the rooms are very open, it would take him two seconds to escape. Obviously, as a pet owner, I was very careful, but it ends up being stressful. They didn't weigh the cat or even look at him properly, just to take advantage of the consultation fee, which isn't exactly cheap after all.

The clinic has everything to be good, however:
- If you come at night, be prepared to wait hours to be seen, as there is only 1 doctor on duty.
- If you have tests done, you have to keep on top of it to get the results. It's common for them to tell you that the results are out, but they don't appear in the app.
- They canceled the telephone service and the WhatsApp service is slow and doesn't have accurate information, such as which doctor will be on duty on which days of the week.
- The local parking lot is closed at night, so we have to leave the car on the street.

Peaceful environment and good staff.
